<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="שבט_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518916723_theRebbe_111" batchId="meluket-_D7_A9_D7_91_D7_98_meluket__BH_POST_1766518916723_theRebbe_111__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the planks of the Mishkan are called "standing" like pillars, analogous to mitzvos which connect Ein Sof to the worlds, yet the planks are only similar to mitzvos, not identical, as mitzvos are rooted above while planks connect from below.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, in the maamar</t>
    <t s="2">(in section 9'20)</t>
    <t s="3">it explains that this is also why the planks are called "standing" (omdim),</t>
    <t s="4">as it is written11</t>
    <t s="5">"And you shall make the planks for the Mishkan of acacia wood, standing" (omdim),</t>
    <t s="6">and it explains that "standing" refers to pillars (amudim),</t>
    <t s="7">the letters of one are like the letters of the other,</t>
    <t s="8">and as it is brought in Maseches Yoma21</t>
    <t s="9">on the verse "acacia wood, standing" that "standing" refers to "that which stand up" (maamidim),</t>
    <t s="10">and it explains in the maamar that the concept of a pillar is that it connects the roof and the floor to be truly as one,</t>
    <t s="11">and this is the concept of the planks which are called pillars,</t>
    <t s="12">which is analogous to the concept of the mitzvos which are called pillars,</t>
    <t s="13">because they draw down and connect Ein Sof blessed He with the worlds truly,</t>
    <t s="14">so too the planks connect Ein Sof blessed He with the worlds.</t>
    <t s="15">Now, regarding the matter of mitzvos being pillars, the Alter Rebbe explains in Iggeres HaKodesh22</t>
    <t s="16">that the Supernal Will is called Kesser,</t>
    <t s="17">and it is brought in the prayer of Rabbi Nechunyah ben HaKaneh23</t>
    <t s="18">that in the crown there are 620 pillars of light.</t>
    <t s="19">And he explains this,</t>
    <t s="20">that just as there are pillars in a great walled house, planted in the earth with their heads connected to the ceiling,</t>
    <t s="21">so too the mitzvos are planted from the height of the levels, which is the Supernal Will blessed He, and are drawn down to the earth,</t>
    <t s="22">that the mitzvos are clothed in physicality, and even the mitzvos that are not clothed in physicality are given to a physical human who has free choice to incline his heart to good, etc.</t>
    <t s="23">Now, from the precise language of the maamar it is understood that there is a difference between the planks and the mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="24">for this is what is said in the maamar, that the planks are "on the order of" (al derech) the mitzvos</t>
    <t s="25">(only as an analogy and example),</t>
    <t s="26">that the mitzvos are actual pillars, while the planks are on the order of the mitzvos.</t>
    <t s="27">Therefore, regarding the mitzvos it uses the language "draw down and connect Ein Sof blessed He and the worlds," but regarding the planks it does not use the language "draw down,"</t>
    <t s="28">only that they connect Ein Sof blessed He with the worlds on the order of the mitzvos.</t>
    <t s="29">Now, in Tanya there is also a difference between the analogy of pillars and the analogue of mitzvos.</t>
    <t s="30">For regarding the pillars it says they are planted in the earth and their heads are connected to the ceiling, but in the analogue of mitzvos it says they are planted in the height and drawn down to the earth.</t>
    <t s="31">Now, the difference between the analogy and the analogue is understood simply,</t>
    <t s="32">for the pillars, their beginning is that they are planted in the earth, and from there they reach the ceiling,</t>
    <t s="33">but not so the mitzvos, for they are planted above,</t>
    <t s="34">as it is said "Who sanctified us with His mitzvos," His mitzvos which are above,</t>
    <t s="35">and from there they are drawn downward.</t>
    <t s="36">And this corresponds to the known rule24</t>
    <t s="37">that there is a difference between a foundation below and a foundation above,</t>
    <t s="38">that below, the foundation is at the bottom and upon it the building is built,</t>
    <t s="39">while above, the foundation is above the building,</t>
    <t s="40">therefore regarding the pillars it says they are "planted" (nitzavim) in the earth,</t>
    <t s="41">for "planted" (nitzav) refers to the strength of the thing,</t>
    <t s="42">like "the king standing" (nitzav melech)25,</t>
    <t s="43">here below, the strength and foundation of the thing is below in the earth, and upon it the building is built,</t>
    <t s="44">while regarding the mitzvos it says they are planted in the height of the levels,</t>
    <t s="45">because above, the strength and foundation of the thing is above.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains why the foundation below differs from the foundation above, based on the concept of "yesh hanivra" (the created entity) which, because it originates from Atzmus (the Essence), will ultimately reveal its true root as the true "yesh" with no cause, and thus the lowest world is the foundation.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">However, this itself needs to be understood,</t>
    <t s="2">why is the foundation below in one manner and the foundation above in another?</t>
    <t s="3">And this will be understood based on what is explained in several matters, among them the matter of "yesh hanivra" (the created entity)26,</t>
    <t s="4">that the fact that in its own perception it has no cause or antecedent, heaven forbid,</t>
    <t s="5">is because its coming into being is from the Essence (Atzmus),</t>
    <t s="6">whose existence is from Its own Self and has no cause or antecedent, heaven forbid, for He alone, by His power and ability, can bring into being something from absolute nothing and non-being,</t>
    <t s="7">as explained in Iggeres HaKodesh27.</t>
    <t s="8">Therefore, in the future, when the truth and innerness of all matters will be revealed, then there will be revealed in the created entity its true root,</t>
    <t s="9">which is the true "yesh" that has no cause or antecedent.</t>
    <t s="10">And with this will be understood what is said that "their beginning is wedged in their end"28,</t>
    <t s="11">that specifically in their end is wedged the beginning, which is above the aspect of "head" (beginning),</t>
    <t s="12">that the beginning, which is the Essence (Atzmus), is found specifically in the aspect of the end,</t>
    <t s="13">in the physical "yesh" beneath which there is no lower level,</t>
    <t s="14">it is specifically a dwelling place for His Essence29,</t>
    <t s="15">which in the future will be revealed,</t>
    <t s="16">and in truth, even now it is so.</t>
    <t s="17">And this is the reason that below, the foundation is specifically below, i.e., Asiyah, and upon it the upper worlds are built,</t>
    <t s="18">unlike above, for it is explained in Tanya30</t>
    <t s="19">that the inner intention is not in the upper worlds, and they are only a radiation, and their entire purpose is only that through them the inner intention be completed specifically below.</t>
    <t s="20">And light and radiation that are higher are more elevated,</t>
    <t s="21">therefore above, the pillars are planted in the height of the levels,</t>
    <t s="22">because the foundation and strength of the thing is above, and from there it is drawn downward.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains, using three analogies of a torch, a barrel, and a drop of seed, that the highest descends specifically to the lowest, revealing the Essence (Atzmus) in the physical world of Asiyah, particularly in physical mitzvos.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">However, it still needs to be understood,</t>
    <t s="2">why is it that specifically in the created entity (yesh hanivra) is the true "yesh," and it is not found in spirituality?</t>
    <t s="3">For ostensibly, the true "yesh" should be in the spirituality of matters and in spiritual matters,</t>
    <t s="4">which is why they are called "upper" because they are elevated in level.</t>
    <t s="5">But the matter is as explained by the Mitteler Rebbe, of blessed memory31,</t>
    <t s="6">three analogies regarding the concept that "the highest of the high descends and is clothed and revealed in the lowest of the low."</t>
    <t s="7">The first analogy is of a large torch whose light is great and shines to a distance,</t>
    <t s="8">and when one needs to illuminate a distant place, a large torch is needed.</t>
    <t s="9">Thus it is understood that in order for the superiority of the large torch to be recognized</t>
    <t s="10">(one brings out its superiority)</t>
    <t s="11">over the superiority of a candle or small torch,</t>
    <t s="12">it is specifically in the distant place,</t>
    <t s="13">there specifically the aspect of "the high" in the torch is revealed.</t>
    <t s="14">For although the light that shines to a distance is a very small light,</t>
    <t s="15">to the extent that if one were to light a candle there, it would shine more than the light of the torch that shines there,</t>
    <t s="16">nevertheless, specifically through this the superiority and power of the torch is recognized.</t>
    <t s="17">And the second analogy is of a barrel full of water,</t>
    <t s="18">or a sage full of wisdom,</t>
    <t s="19">that due to the abundance of water in the barrel that is filled to overflowing, from this it spills out also outside,</t>
    <t s="20">and specifically through this the abundance of water is recognized.</t>
    <t s="21">For although the water that spills outside is ownerless and small in quantity relative to the water inside the barrel,</t>
    <t s="22">nevertheless, specifically through this it is recognized that the barrel is filled to overflowing.</t>
    <t s="23">And so it is also regarding wisdom,</t>
    <t s="24">that through the aspect of "nivlelos hachochmah" (the fallen fruits of wisdom) and on the order of32</t>
    <t s="25">"the casual conversation of Torah scholars,"</t>
    <t s="26">specifically through this it is recognized that the drawing down is from a great sage who is connected to the depth of wisdom33.</t>
    <t s="27">And the third analogy is of the influence of the physical drop from which procreation occurs, from one essence to another essence,</t>
    <t s="28">a new essence,</t>
    <t s="29">unlike the influence of intellect, which is a spiritual influence, where it is impossible to have a new procreation,</t>
    <t s="30">and only when the student is intelligent will he then understand the intellect that the teacher influenced him.</t>
    <t s="31">Thus it is understood the superiority of the physical drop specifically,</t>
    <t s="32">that specifically from it a new essence is born,</t>
    <t s="33">an essence different from the first essence,</t>
    <t s="34">which is the influence of the child.</t>
    <t s="35">And it can be said in another way in explanation of the three analogies,</t>
    <t s="36">that the concept of "the highest of the high descends to the lowest of the low"</t>
    <t s="37">is the drawing down from the Essence (Atzmus) to Biyah (Beri'ah, Yetzirah, Asiyah).</t>
    <t s="38">For in Atzilus, "He and His life are one, He and His limbs are one"34,</t>
    <t s="39">and it is called the world of Elokus (Godliness)35,</t>
    <t s="40">and it is not low,</t>
    <t s="41">and the intention of the term "low" is the matter of Beri'ah,</t>
    <t s="42">which is the worlds of Biyah.</t>
    <t s="43">Now, the order of the drawing down in the worlds of Biyah is in the manner of "or, mayim, v'rakia" (fire, water, and firmament)36,</t>
    <t s="44">as explained at length in the maamarim of the month of Tishrei37.</t>
    <t s="45">And this is the concept of the three analogies,</t>
    <t s="46">for the analogy of the torch is the aspect of fire (or),</t>
    <t s="47">and the analogy of the barrel is the aspect of water (mayim),</t>
    <t s="48">and the analogy of the drop is the aspect of the firmament (rakia),</t>
    <t s="49">which becomes a physical substance and a new essence,</t>
    <t s="50">and therefore "water that has been exposed" is nullified from the law of drawn water, to the extent that according to some opinions it may be raised and does not invalidate,</t>
    <t s="51">and it can be used to form a mikveh ab initio38.</t>
    <t s="52">Now, it was explained in the discourses of the month of Tishrei37</t>
    <t s="53">that the aspect of "or, mayim, v'rakia" exists not only in Biyah but also in Atzilus and in Kesser and higher36,</t>
    <t s="54">even in the light before the tzimtzum (contraction)39.</t>
    <t s="55">Thus it is understood that there too all three analogies of the torch,</t>
    <t s="56">barrel, and drop apply.</t>
    <t s="57">And in every place and every level, the revelation of the highest of the high is in the lowest of the low</t>
    <t s="58">(meaning that in the lowest of that world, the highest of that world is revealed).</t>
    <t s="59">Now, in the overall order of the chain of descent, the lowest of the low is in Biyah, down to the world of Asiyah,</t>
    <t s="60">there the highest of the high is revealed,</t>
    <t s="61">which is above the highest of the high relative to Atzilus and above Atzilus and before the tzimtzum,</t>
    <t s="62">which is His Essence and Being,</t>
    <t s="63">it is revealed in the lowest of the low,</t>
    <t s="64">for the double language "lowest of the low" indicates the most low possible,</t>
    <t s="65">beneath which there is no lower,</t>
    <t s="66">and this is the world of Asiyah.</t>
    <t s="67">And this is the concept that the pillars are planted specifically in the earth,</t>
    <t s="68">for when one needs to build a great walled house, which is the concept of the greatness of G-d,</t>
    <t s="69">for "in the place of His greatness, there you find His humility"40,</t>
    <t s="70">now, in the entire order of the chain of descent, even though there is an aspect of "or, mayim, v'rakia" in all levels,</t>
    <t s="71">but in order for there to be a revelation of the highest of the high, which is the Essence (Atzmus), its revelation is specifically in the lowest of the low, which is the world of Asiyah,</t>
    <t s="72">and within Asiyah itself, not in spiritual Asiyah, but in physical Asiyah.</t>
    <t s="73">And from this it is understood that even within physical Asiyah itself, there must also be the lowest of the low,</t>
    <t s="74">meaning that the revelation of the Essence (Atzmus) is not in the spiritual service in this world, but specifically in physical Asiyah.</t>
    <t s="75">And this is also what is precise in Likkutei Torah in the discourses on Tzitzis41</t>
    <t s="76">in the analogy of the pillars that are planted in the earth,</t>
    <t s="77">that in order for the pillars to hold up the building and the ceiling above them,</t>
    <t s="78">they must be specifically in hard earth, not in loose soil,</t>
    <t s="79">so too the mitzvos must be specifically in hard earth,</t>
    <t s="80">and as he concludes there41</t>
    <t s="81">"Asiyah above,"</t>
    <t s="82">which is the mitzvos that are specifically clothed in physicality.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
